snippet.title: 20 UK Tinned Foods You Must Stock Up On Before 2026 Ends
snippet.description:
20 UK Canned Foods You Must Stock Up On Before 2026 Ends

Most British shoppers treat the date on a tin as an instruction. It passes, the tin goes in the bin, and another one goes in the trolley next week without anyone thinking about it.

But when you look at what that date legally means, what the Food Standards Agency actually says about it, and what happens inside a sealed tin over years rather than months, it becomes clear that a great deal of perfectly good food is being thrown away on the strength of a number that was never about safety.

In this video, we investigate the tins on British shelves and ask one simple question: which of these will still be sound long after the label says otherwise, and which are worth buying at this year's prices?

In this video, you'll discover:

What the date printed on a tin legally means, and the different date that does concern your safety
What chemists found when they opened food that had spent over a century underwater
Three reasons the printed date is far shorter than the contents actually need
The one item covered here that should be rotated rather than stored and forgotten
The signs that mean a tin goes in the bin whatever its date says
The five-second check that tells you whether what's at the back of your cupboard is still good

Every claim in this video is based on current labels, supermarket listings, company information, public records, or named sources.

At UK Food Exposed, we investigate what British consumers are actually getting for their money, from supermarket shelves to restaurant chains and the heritage brands we grew up trusting. Nobody in the supply chain loses when a good tin goes in the bin, which is exactly why nobody explains the difference.

If this video helps you shop smarter, subscribe to UK Food Exposed, hit the Hype button, and hit like. Every hype helps push this investigation to more shoppers before they waste money on packaging, nostalgia, or marketing that does less than it promises.

snippet.title: Seven Days Until the Apocalypse… Here’s What I Did?
snippet.description:
DISCLAIMER: This is a fictional "what if" scenario created for entertainment purposes only. This story is not based on real events. It is a creative exploration of a hypothetical zombie outbreak survival situation. Viewer discretion is advised. 

I had exactly 7 days to prepare for the zombie apocalypse — and I used every single one of them. This is my zombie outbreak survival story, how I turned a suburban home into a fortress before the world collapsed around me.

Here is Part 2- https://youtu.be/1bEPB4AdzQg

When a contact from a military researsh base calld me with classified information about an aggressive pathogen spreading through the population, I didn't panic. I calculated. As a supply chain logistics coordinator, I understood better than anyone how fast the trucks would stop, how quickly the shelves would empty, and how thin the line was between civilization and chaos. 

This zombie apocalypse preparation story follows every decision I made — from boarding windows and stockpiling months of food to the impossible moral choices that haunted me long after the outbreak began.

TIMESTAMPS:

0:00 — The Phone Call That Changed Everything
3:45 — Day 7: The Warning — "You Have Seven Days"
8:20 — Day 6: First Supply Run — Stockpiling Begins
14:30 — Day 5: Boarding the Windows & Buying Weapons
21:00 — Day 4: The Shelves Are Already Empty
27:15 — Day 3: Military Convoy in the Neighborhood
33:40 — Day 2: The Last Normal Day — Final Preparations
40:00 — Day 1: Power Flickering — The World Is Ending
45:30 — Day Zero: The Power Goes Out Forever
50:15 — The First Screams — The Outbreak Hits Our Street
55:00 — The Woman at the Door — The Decision That Haunts Me
1:00:00 — Weeks of Silence — Surviving Inside the Sealed House
1:07:30 — Contact With Neighbors — A Light in the Darkness
1:14:00 — The Radio — We're Not Alone
1:20:00 — Day 61: Leaving the Fortress — The Drive to Safety
1:27:00 — Arrival at the Safe Zone — What Survival Really Means


I spent 61 days sealed inside a boarded-up house with my girlfriend Elena, rationing food and water down to the calorie, living in complete darkness and silence while the infected roamed the streets outside. Every decision was a calculation — how many days of water remained, how many cans of food per person, how much noise was too much. But the hardest calclations weren't about supplies. They were about people.

I didn't call my brother for six days. I didn't open the door when a mther and her child begged for help. I optimized for survival so completely that survival itself became the thing I had to survive.

This apocalypse survival story explres what happens when an ordinary person with logistics expertise gets advance warning of a zombie outbreak and has to make impossible choices — who to save, who to leave behind, and whether the math that keeps you alive is worth the cost of following it.

WHAT YOU'LL EXPERIENCE IN THIS VIDEO:

• Realistic zombie outbreak preparation — day-by-day brekdown
• Home fortification and survival supply planning
• The psychological toll of long-term isolation
• Moral dilemmas with no right answers
• First-person immersive storytelling
• Post-apocalyptic journey to a safe zone

snippet.title: What I Carry Every Day in Downtown LA
snippet.description:
I break down my real urban EDC setup for Downtown LA, the everyday carry items I keep on me to handle normal city problems before they turn into bigger ones. This is not a bug-out bag, tactical loadout, or apocalypse kit. It’s a practical pocket EDC system for real life in the city.

snippet.title: 10 Cheap Household Items That Still Work When the Grid Goes Down
snippet.description:
Most people picture a grid failure as something that happens elsewhere until a storm, substation fire, or cyberattack plunges connected households into sudden darkness without heat, water, or refrigeration. Historical events like the 1989 Quebec blackout and the massive Carrington Event of 1859 demonstrate how vulnerable modern infrastructure is to severe geomagnetic storms and grid stress. While major events carry catastrophic potential, mundane failures like ice storms and heat waves also expose how quickly modern comforts collapse when the power stops. Fortunately, closing the preparedness gap does not require expensive bunkers or generators. This video explores ten highly effective, incredibly affordable items costing between one and thirty dollars that function entirely without electricity, providing essential solutions for fire-starting, cooking, thermal insulation, emergency lighting, and basic electromagnetic pulse protection.

Discover why simple items like petroleum jelly-soaked cotton balls, cast iron skillets, aluminum foil, strike-anywhere matches, galvanized steel trash cans, duct tape, wool scarves, cardboard, knee-high socks, and tealight candles form a reliable, interconnected survival system. Watch until the end to understand the underlying physics of each item and learn how a small investment today can protect your household before the next major outage hits.

snippet.title: You Have 60 Minutes After The Grid Fails — Here's What To Do
snippet.description:
When the power grid fails, you don't get a warning. No siren, no announcement — just silence. And the first 60 minutes after the grid goes down quietly decide whether you stay calm and prepared, or end up in the panic with everyone else. This is exactly what happens in that first hour, minute by minute, and what to do while there's still time.
Most people waste the most important hour of their lives standing in the kitchen, flipping a dead light switch, waiting for someone to fix a world that already changed. This video breaks down the real, grounded sequence of a grid-down event — what dies instantly, what dies next, and the calm, simple moves that put you 45 minutes ahead of your entire neighborhood before the crowd even wakes up.
We cover the traffic and road cascade in the first five minutes, why your phone shows full bars but can't connect, the silent countdown on your water supply, the moment money and gas pumps stop working, and the exact tipping point when your whole town panics at once — plus what a prepared person is doing in each of those windows.
This isn't fear-mongering and it isn't political. It's survival science, infrastructure reality, and human psychology — the way the lights actually go out.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT THIS VIDEO WILL GIVE YOU
By the end of this video, you'll know:
– What systems fail in the first 5 minutes — and why the danger isn't the dark
– Why your phone lies to you with full signal bars, and the one message to send before the network jams
– How long your tap water really lasts after the pumps stop, and why "I'll boil it later" is a bad bet
– Why a full gas station becomes useless the instant the grid drops
– The exact moment your town stops being calm — and how to be finished before the panic wave hits
– The simple, free actions that separate the prepared from the desperate in the first hour
– A clear, repeatable 60-minute mindset you can actually use, not a gear list you'll never remember
This is the head start almost nobody knows they're being handed.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SOURCES & REFERENCES
This video is built on publicly available guidance and established science, including:
– FEMA and Ready.gov emergency preparedness and power outage guidance
– U.S. Department of Energy and NERC material on grid reliability, load shedding, and cascading failures
– FCC regulations and reporting on cell-site backup power and network behavior during outages
– American Water Works Association (AWWA) information on electric pumping, distribution pressure, and water storage
– EPA drinking water guidance on pressure loss, contamination risk, and boil-water advisories
– CISA / Department of Homeland Security material on critical infrastructure interdependencies
– Published research on normalcy bias, crowd behavior, and collective decision-making during disasters
All survival analysis is based on realistic physics, engineering, and human psychology. Nothing here is dramatized beyond what the systems actually do.

snippet.title: Decades of Survival Gear Testing Came Down to THIS❗️
snippet.description:
Survival gear, survival tools, bug out bag essentials, 72-hour emergency kit, EDC gear and emergency preparedness — after decades of testing and spending thousands of dollars on gear, I want to help save YOU money.

This is Jason Salyer with ON3. After decades of buying survival gear with my own money, testing it, using it and abusing it in the real world, these are the survival tools that have actually earned their place.

I’ve spent thousands figuring out what works — and what doesn’t — so hopefully you don’t have to.

If you’re building a bug out bag, go bag, get-home bag, 72-hour survival kit, emergency survival kit, vehicle emergency kit or simply looking for practical survival gear and supplies, I’m showing you equipment I actually use and trust.

But let’s be realistic about the whole “bug out bag” idea.

Chances are you’re probably never going to grab a backpack and disappear into the wilderness. That’s why I don’t want survival gear sitting untouched in a bag waiting for SHTF.

SURVIVAL GEAR SHOULD EARN ITS PLACE.

I use this gear around my homestead. I use it working in the field, hunting, camping, traveling and doing handyman work — the same kinds of jobs blue-collar workers, outdoorsmen and homeowners deal with every day.

And if there IS a natural disaster, power outage, evacuation or emergency, much of this same equipment can go directly into your bug out bag, 72-hour emergency kit, get-home bag, go bag or vehicle emergency kit.

Don’t buy gear for a fantasy.

Buy useful tools that make you more capable TODAY and can help you when things go wrong.

In this video, I’m breaking down some of the best survival gear and emergency preparedness supplies I’ve found through decades of real-world testing, including Refuge Medical first aid gear and medical supplies, my EDC knife and cutting tools, water filtration and water purification, fire-starting gear, emergency tools, survival equipment and everyday carry gear.

Water. Fire. First aid. Cutting tools. EDC. Emergency preparedness.

These aren’t just items on a bug out bag checklist. They’re tools you can actually use.

Some are inexpensive. Some I’ve carried for years. And some can potentially save you hundreds or even thousands of dollars.

I’ve bought gear that looked great but didn’t hold up. I’ve tested equipment in the woods, on the homestead and in the field. I’ve gotten it wet, dirty, dropped it, beaten it up and actually USED it.

Hopefully the thousands of dollars I’ve spent and decades I’ve spent testing this stuff can save you from making the same expensive mistakes.

This isn’t another “50 survival gadgets you need before SHTF” video.

You don’t need a backpack full of gadgets.

You need dependable tools and the skills to use them.

Whether you’re searching for the best survival gear, bug out bag essentials, 72-hour survival kit, emergency preparedness gear, emergency supplies, emergency survival kit, EDC gear, everyday carry, get-home bag, go bag, first aid kit, water filter, water purification or practical survival tools, these are the kinds of items I believe are actually worth owning.

The best survival gear isn’t equipment that sits untouched until an emergency. It’s gear you’ve already used enough that when something DOES go wrong, you know exactly how to use it.

And remember — the most important survival tool isn’t something you can buy.

It’s your knowledge, skills and experience.

I’m Jason Salyer with ON3. I’ve worked as a Human Performance Specialist with Naval Special Warfare, served as a Division I Head Strength & Conditioning Coach, and survived 30 days with no tools on History Channel’s Alone: The Beast.

ON3 is about practical preparedness, survival skills, self-reliance and field-tested survival gear that works when you need it.

Are grocery prices about to climb again? Discover 9 foods to stock up on before November 2026 as rising food costs, supply chain disruptions, agricultural challenges, and seasonal Thanksgiving demand put pressure on America's grocery stores.
From record-high coffee prices and historically low U.S. cattle inventories to bird flu concerns affecting turkey production, several everyday groceries face supply and pricing challenges heading into the holiday season.
But this isn't about panic buying or predicting empty supermarkets.
It's about smart grocery shopping, emergency food storage, protecting your food budget, and preparing before prices rise or your favorite products become harder to find.
In this Homestead Roots video, we're breaking down 9 groceries facing potential price increases or reduced availability, the reasons behind those pressures, and practical ways to prepare your pantry without overspending.
And don't miss #1 — an ancient food prized for thousands of years that stores exceptionally well and may deserve a permanent place in your pantry!

📈 WHY GROCERY PRICES MAY KEEP RISING
Food prices are influenced by more than what happens inside your local grocery store.
🌾 Fertilizer and fuel costs affect farming expenses.
🚚 Shipping disruptions increase transportation costs.
🐄 Smaller livestock herds limit meat supply.
🐝 Agricultural diseases affect crops and pollinators.
🦃 Avian influenza affects poultry production.
🏭 Packaging costs influence canned food prices.
🛢️ Biofuel production competes for vegetable oils.
🛒 Thanksgiving and holiday shopping increase seasonal demand.
These challenges don't mean all nine foods will disappear. They can mean higher prices, fewer choices, or temporary shortages of certain products.

You don't need to panic buy or spend hundreds of dollars in one shopping trip.
Start with a simple plan:
✅ Buy two extra pantry staples on each grocery trip.
✅ Focus on foods your family already eats.
✅ Watch weekly sales and compare unit prices.
✅ Freeze nuts, meat, and other suitable foods.
✅ Store grains in appropriate food-safe containers.
✅ Rotate canned goods using the oldest first.
✅ Keep cooking oil in a cool, dark place.
✅ Purchase pure honey from trusted sources.
✅ Support local farmers, growers, and beekeepers.
A reliable pantry is built gradually, not through fear.

Why do survivalists, bushcrafters, backpackers, hikers, campers, and preppers obsess over this?
Because this is fatwood, one of the best natural fire starters you can carry. You can often find it in the wild. I always keep a piece inside my Hill People Gear Kit Bag and my ultralight 72 hour survival kit. snippet.title: You Only Need These 6 Canned Foods to Survive Hard Times!
snippet.description:
What if your pantry is full, but still not prepared for a genuinely difficult month? This video reveals 6 canned foods that can make a pantry far more practical—from canned fruit and potatoes to tomatoes, chicken, sardines and beans.

Each food has a specific purpose. Canned potatoes provide an already-cooked starch, canned tomatoes can turn basic ingredients into complete meals, while canned chicken delivers ready-to-use protein with almost no preparation. Sardines add concentrated nutrition, and canned beans can stretch expensive ingredients across more servings.

The key isn't buying huge quantities. It's choosing foods your household will actually eat, rotating your supply and building a pantry around everyday meals—not just emergencies.

From foods costing under a dollar to practical shelf-stable staples, these six cans can help make your grocery budget go further while keeping meals simple.
